messages:
eli: Heads-up — saw a sudden spike of 503s 13:12-13:15 UTC from hosted inference. Root cause looks like a rapid sequence of upstream worker SIGKILLs, multiple containers dying within seconds. Customer impact: increased latency + timeouts.
maya: Which fleet/cluster? any pattern by model or request size?
eli: Canary in eu-west-1 small pool (hosted-infer-canary-2). Mostly requests with long context (8k) hitting the same runner image. Not all requests fail, seems bursty.
ops-oncall: infra-bot posted autoscaler events at the time? can you paste logs?
infra-bot: [auto] detected 8 container restarts in hosted-infer-canary-2 between 13:11:40 and 13:14:58. Restart reason: Killed (SIGKILL).
support-led: Customer reported 40% increase in 503s for their org. They hit us with a queued batch (high concurrency). Billing is asking for ticket flag.
john: Quick triage — SIGKILL often OOM or host preemption. Any OOM logs from kernel or containerd?
maya: grabbed kube events and kernel dmesg from the node:
```
Mar 17 13:12:02 host-78 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 32456 (infer-runner) score 982 or sacrifice child
Mar 17 13:12:02 host-78 kernel: Killed process 32456 (infer-runner) total-vm:9200000kB, anon-rss:7800000kB, file-rss:0kB
```
and containerd: `task infer-runner[32456] killed by signal 9`
eli: but we also see a second sequence a minute later with SIGKILLs without clear OOM lines — could be cgroup OOM vs host-level preemptions. Node was also reporting GPU preemption events.
sasha: Are these preemptions from the cloud host (spot reclaim) or from our evictor? Check metadata: node flagged preemptible=true and had a recent maintenance tag.
ops-oncall: Confirmed: node host-78 had a cloud maintenance trigger at 13:11:45 and VM was force-stopped shortly after. That would explain abrupt SIGKILLs.
john: Actionable next steps: 1) temporarily rotate traffic away from hosted-infer-canary-2 to fallback routing policy; 2) enable soft-fallback to smaller-context variant for this customer's org; 3) collect full core + logs for one of the crashed pods.
maya: repro attempt: running `ab -n 200 -c 40` against canary endpoint with 8k contexts reproduces higher crash rate when hitting that node. Steps in runbook:
```
# find crashed pod
kubectl get pods -n hosted | grep infer-runner-canary
kubectl logs -n hosted <pod> --previous
kubectl exec -n hosted <pod> -- ls /var/crash || true
# collect node dmesg
gcloud compute ssh host-78 -- 'dmesg | tail -n 200' > host-78-dmesg.log
```
support-led: I've notified the customer that we're investigating. They asked if we can apply immediate mitigations — prefer routing to Dedicated if available.
ops-oncall: Implemented routing override: moved 30% of canary traffic to eu-west-1-fallback. Monitoring now.
infra-bot: [auto] routing override enacted at 13:24:11 UTC by ops-oncall.
eli: Monitoring dashboards show 503s dropped to baseline after routing change. Need postmortem: why did scheduled maintenance land on a host with active canary capacity? also need to make host preemption safer (graceful drain, avoid long-context on preemptible nodes).
john: Follow-ups: - Add node tag to avoid long-context scheduling (affinity/taint). - Ensure our autoscaler drains nodes on preempt notice (watch metadata). - Add runbook step to failover long-context requests sooner.
sasha: I'll open a tracked ticket and attach logs + core dumps path.
maya: saving logs to gs://redwood-incident-logs/4311112222/ (dmesg, kube-events, pod-logs, core.tar.gz).
support-led: Customer update sent: temporary routing applied, full postmortem within 24h. They acknowledged. :thumbsup:
eli: good. Marking incident as mitigated. Will follow up with postmortem doc and scheduling changes.
